chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Salih ibn Razin, from Shihab who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman for one thousand dirhams, so he paid it to her, and she gifted it to him and said, 'I am desirous of you.' So he divorced her before entering with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He returns to her five hundred dirhams.'

key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: Dirham, a silver coin used as currency for dowry

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning the dowry if a husband divorces his wife before consummation after she gifted him the full amount?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that the standard Quranic ruling of returning half the dower upon pre-consummation divorce applies even if the wife had previously gifted the full amount back to the husband. It highlights the juristic principle that the 'gift' (hibah) is distinct from the 'dower' (mahr), ensuring the wife retains her statutory right to half the original agreed value. This ruling underscores the protection of women's financial rights in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between voluntary transfer of wealth and the legal obligation of mahr.
